newsitem.title: USA: Cigna to buy Healthsource for $1.7 billion.
newsitem.headline: Cigna to buy Healthsource for $1.7 billion.

text.p: Cigna Corp. said Friday it signed a definitive agreement to acquire Healthsource Inc. for about $1.7 billon in cash.
Cigna, a leading nationwide provider of healthcare insurance, said it would begin a tender offer for all Healthsource shares at $21.75 a share within five business days.
Based on Healthsource's closing price of $16.50 on the New York Stock Exchange Thursday, the offering price represents a 32 percent premium for Heathsource shares.
Healthsource stock jumped $4 to $20.875 in consolidated trading on the New York Stock Exchange.
A health maintenence organisation based in Hooksett, N.H., Healthsource posted a 1996 net loss of $5 million, including special charges of $35 million. It had total revenues of $438.3 million.
The company, which operates HMOs in the Northeast and the South, has premiums and premium equivalents worth about $3.8 billion.

"Health care is our largest and most profitable business, and this transaction will further strengthen our operation to the benefit of our shareholders," Cigna Chief Executive Wilson Taylor said in a statement.

The proposed acquisition gives Cigna greater bargaining power in the intensely competitive health insurance business as well as a significant new presence in several key markets, analysts said after the deal was announced.
Cigna also solidified its position as a health insurance consolidator and is likely to pursue additional deals, analysts said.
"They've laid the groundwork for a stronger health care operation with this transaction," A.M. Best senior vice president Larry Mayewski said.
But this was not likely to be Cigna's last health insurance deal, analysts said.
"I don't think this will be the end of things," said Mark Puccia, director of Standard & Poor's insurance rating services. "Cigna is committed to the managed care marketplace," he said.
The deal comes nearly a year after Aetna Inc. agreed to buy U.S. Healthcare for $8.9 billion in a move that put its health care rivals on competitive notice.
"There's no doubt that when Aetna bought U.S. Healthcare, they raised the competitive hurdles," Mayewski said.
Philadelphia-based Cigna, which operates in all 50 states, offers medical, dental, disability and life insurance products, with 1996 assets of $99 billion and revenues of $19 billion.

"We expect this acquisition to contribute to increased earnings upon full integration, which is targeted for 1998," Taylor said. "We believe there are potential pre-tax cost savings of more than $75 million associated with the integration."
Taylor also said Cigna expected to see revenue and earnings growth through efficiencies gained by the deal, which includes payment of $250 million of outstanding Healthsource long-term debt.
Once the acquisition is completed, Cigna said, the new Cigna Healthcare unit will operate HMOs with 5.3 million members and will cover 7 million people with its medical indemnity business.
Cigna's stock closed up 25 cents at $152.875 on the NYSE.
